note: Positive D5. Cobra at the pin only READS pflag's Deprecated field, it never sets it: nonCompletableFlag (bash_completions.go:700) hides flags with len(flag.Deprecated)>0, doc/man_docs.go:161 and doc/yaml_docs.go:154-156 skip them in generated docs. The operation itself, FlagSet.MarkDeprecated, appears at the pin only in test files (command_test.go:2178, bash_completions_test.go:250) and is a pflag method, and A2 explicitly rules out test assertions and relation-only citations. No tracked, regular, non-test .go span contains the value/operation asked for, so A2 fails on a positive finding about the pinned bytes, not on search effort. (D3 would also fit, since the marking operation lives in the pflag dependency, but I did not read that dependency and so rest the rejection on in-tree evidence only.)

Positive D4. The pinned tree implements no licence-key capability of any kind. A case-insensitive git grep for 'license'/'licence' over tracked .go and .md files at the pin returns only Apache-2.0 header comments, the README 'License' section pointing at LICENSE.txt, and one line inside a copied cobra-cli help sample in site/content/user_guide.md ('-l, --license string   name of license for the project') which is illustrative output, not a cobra feature; there is no key generation, storage, validation, entitlement or activation code anywhere. What the pin does implement is a command/flag/completion framework (command.go, args.go, flag_groups.go, completions.go), so the honest answer is only that Cobra does not provide the requested capability and any key management would be the caller's own code. Section 4 forbids converting that absence into a grade-3 span.

judgements.anchor: if err := c.RunE(c, argWoFlags); err != nil {
judgements.reason: The primary result channel: an error returned by the subcommand's RunE ends execute() at once and is handed back up, which is how a subcommand's outcome reaches whatever invoked the tree.

The parent-facing mechanism: after the subcommand runs, cobra walks from the executed command up through its parents and calls the first PersistentPostRun/PersistentPostRunE it finds (or all of them when EnableTraverseRunHooks is set), passing the executed child command and its args. That is how a parent observes a subcommand's completion and, through that same *Command, whatever it recorded.
The operation for attaching the result itself: the child stores it on its own command context, which the parent's persistent post-run hook reads back from the child command it is handed.
ExecuteC returns both the executed subcommand and its error to the root caller, giving a second route to the subcommand's outcome.
Declares the error-returning body a subcommand must use for its result to propagate at all.

note: A1-A4 hold. Two in-tree routes: return the result as an error from the subcommand's RunE, which execute() propagates so ExecuteC/Execute hand it (together with the executed *Command) back at the root; or have the subcommand record the result on itself (context via SetContext, or Annotations) and read it in the parent's PersistentPostRun/PersistentPostRunE, which cobra calls after the child's Run with the executed child command as its argument.

Positive D4. Nothing in the pinned tree expands, matches or otherwise interprets file globs for flags. A case-insensitive git grep for 'glob' over tracked .go and .md files at the pin matches only the unrelated identifiers Global/globNormFunc/activeHelpGlobal, and ParseFlags (command.go:1818-1841) hands the raw argument vector straight to pflag with no pattern handling of its own. The nearest related facility is completion-side file EXTENSION filtering, not globbing: shell_completions.go MarkFlagFilename/MarkPersistentFlagFilename set the BashCompFilenameExt annotation, and completions.go:66-71 defines ShellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt, whose comment says the values are used as file extension filters; the bash script builds an extglob from that extension list (bash_completions.go:138-147), and fish_completions.go:191 states outright that file extension filtering and directory filtering are not supported there. So the pin supports extension-based completion filters, not flags with file globs, and the honest answer is only that the requested capability is not implemented, which Section 4 forbids converting into a grade-3 span.
